ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The image shows a discrete/control block diagram with input R feeding a first summing junction. The output of that junction passes through a sampled link toward a second summing junction, then through the forward block G to the output C. The output C is fed back along two negative feedback paths: one through H2 to the negative input of the first summing junction, and another through H1 to the negative input of the second summing junction. Thus there are two subtractive feedback signals derived from C, one entering before the sampled intermediate signal and one entering just before G. Reasoning: Define the signal after the first summing junction as E1(z), and define the input to G as U(z). From the first summing junction, the H2 feedback is subtracted, so E1(z)=R(z)-H2 C(z). From the second summing junction, the H1 feedback is also subtracted, so U(z)=E1(z)-H1 C(z). The forward block gives C(z)=G(z)U(z). Substituting E1(z) into U(z), U(z)=R(z)-H2 C(z)-H1 C(z)=R(z)-(H1+H2)C(z). Therefore C(z)=G(z)[R(z)-(H1+H2)C(z)]. Rearranging gives C(z)+G(z)(H1+H2)C(z)=G(z)R(z), so C(z)[1+H1G(z)+H2G(z)]=G(z)R(z). Hence the closed-loop pulse transfer function is C(z)/R(z)=G(z)/(1+H1G(z)+H2G(z)).
